fixes.explanation: Right, baker. The text says, “Pointing to His disciples, He said, ‘Here are My mother and My brothers.’” Disciples are the people who follow Jesus. He points right at them as He says it.

You got it, baker. Some of the scribes, the teachers of the law, and some Pharisees say, “Teacher, we want to see a sign from You.” The text doesn't tell us why they ask. I'll leave that open, because the text does.

That one makes sense if you picture a quiet chat in a corner. But nothing in the text says they ask for a private word. They say to Him, “Teacher, we want to see a sign from You.” The ask is a sign, and a word in private isn't mentioned.

Elijah, a prophet who spoke for the LORD in Israel (1 Kings 18:36), is a big name, so I get the pull. But Jesus doesn't mention him here. He says the sign is that of the prophet Jonah. Elijah's name isn't in these verses, so Jonah is the answer.

Forty days and forty nights is a famous stretch of time. It's how long the rain fell in the flood in the days of Noah (Genesis 7:12). But for Jonah in the great fish, Jesus says three days and three nights. Different story, different number.

Wiser is close to the idea, and I like that you were thinking about wisdom. But Jesus' exact word is “greater.” He says, “…and now One greater than Jonah is here.” Wisdom comes up in the next verse, when He talks about Solomon's wisdom, and there He says One greater than Solomon is here.
Bolder is a fair guess when you're thinking of a preacher. But the word Jesus uses is “greater.” He says, “…and now One greater than Jonah is here.” Boldness isn't mentioned in this verse.

That's the one. Jesus says the Queen of the South “…came from the ends of the earth to hear the wisdom of Solomon…” Solomon was a king of Israel, and people came from every nation to hear his wisdom (1 Kings 4:34). She made a long trip just to listen.
That would be a rough day for the house. But Jesus says the spirit finds it “…vacant, swept clean, and put in order.” Nothing about fire or burning. The house is empty and tidy.

That's right, baker. After the picture of the spirit and the house, Jesus says, “So will it be with this wicked generation.” He ties the picture back to this wicked generation. That's where the whole picture was heading.

Some of the scribes were among those asking for a sign back at the start of this passage, so they're easy to remember. But in this moment, the text says Jesus was “Pointing to His disciples…” His disciples are the ones He calls His mother and brothers.
